square-footage-calculator.quickAnswer: Area = length x width. A 12 ft by 10 ft room is 120 sq ft. Add all your rooms and the tool totals them - three rooms of 120, 96 and 80 sq ft give 296 sq ft - then adds your waste allowance: 10% extra means buying 326 sq ft of flooring.
keyFacts: Area of a rectangle = length x width, measured in the same unit both ways.
1 square meter = 10.764 square feet; 1 square foot = 0.0929 square meters.
Total project area is the simple sum of every room's area - measure each room separately.
The waste allowance (typically 5-15%) covers cutting losses, pattern matching and spare pieces.
Odd shapes: split them into rectangles, measure each, and add the areas.
howTo: Enter a room name, its length and width, then press Add room.
Repeat for every room in the project.
Set the waste allowance percentage (10% is a safe default).
Read the total area in both units and the material quantity to buy.
square-footage-calculator.formula:
Room area = length x width.
Total area = sum of all room areas.
Material to buy = total x (1 + waste / 100).
Conversions: sq m = sq ft x 0.09290304; sq ft = sq m / 0.09290304.
Example: (120 + 96 + 80) x 1.10 = 296 x 1.10 = 325.6 -> 326 sq ft.
square-footage-calculator.workedExample:
Three rooms in feet:
1. Living room: 12 x 10 = 120 sq ft.
2. Bedroom: 12 x 8 = 96 sq ft.
3. Kitchen: 10 x 8 = 80 sq ft.
4. Total: 120 + 96 + 80 = 296 sq ft (= 27.5 sq m).
5. Waste 10%: 296 x 1.10 = 325.6 sq ft.
6. Buy 326 sq ft of flooring.
benefits: Buy the right amount - no expensive shortfall, no wasted surplus.

limitations: Rectangles only - L-shaped or curved rooms must be split into rectangles first.
Waste percentage is a rule of thumb; intricate patterns may need more.
Does not account for doorways, closets or fixtures - subtract those areas yourself.
Material is reported in square feet; convert for suppliers who sell per box or per square meter.

faqs.q: How much waste allowance should I add?
faqs.a: 10% is the safe default for straight-lay flooring. Use 15% for diagonal layouts or patterned tiles, and 5% only for simple large open areas.

faqs.q: How do I measure an L-shaped room?
faqs.a: Split it into two rectangles, measure length x width for each, and add the two areas. The tool totals them when you add both as rooms.
For large openings, yes - measure the doorway area and mentally subtract it, or add the room and reduce the waste percentage slightly.

faqs.q: Can I mix feet and meters?
faqs.a: The unit toggle applies to all rooms. Convert your measurements to one unit first for a consistent total.

faqs.q: What is the difference between sq ft and sq m?
faqs.a: Both are area units: 1 sq m = 10.764 sq ft. The tool shows both totals so you can match any supplier's quote.
No - it gives you the quantity to buy. Multiply by your supplier's per-unit price for the cost.
